Developing Web Applications with KoldFusion

Reusing Code and Sending Mail

As an application grows, the same snippets turn up again and again: a formatted address, a navigation bar, a price calculation. CFINCLUDE (chapter 6) shares code that works with the page's own variables. Custom tags go one step further: they are self-contained, take attributes, and keep their variables to themselves.

Custom tags

A custom tag is an ordinary template. Save it as ch8_greeting.cfm in the same directory as the calling page, or anywhere under the CustomTags directory of the server, and call it as <CF_CH8_GREETING>. Inside the tag, the attributes arrive in the Attributes scope, and the Caller scope reaches the variables of the calling page, which is how a tag hands back results.

ch8_greeting.cfmRun this example · View source
<!--- ch8_greeting.cfm: a custom tag.
      Call it as <CF_CH8_GREETING NAME="..." COLOR="...">.
      Opened on its own, it simply uses its default values. --->
<CFPARAM NAME="Attributes.Name" DEFAULT="World">
<CFPARAM NAME="Attributes.Color" DEFAULT="003399">

<CFOUTPUT>
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica" SIZE="4" COLOR="###Attributes.Color#">
<B>Hello, #HTMLEditFormat(Attributes.Name)#!</B></FONT></P>
</CFOUTPUT>

<!--- Hand a value back to the calling page --->
<CFSET Caller.GreetingTime = TimeFormat(Now(), "h:mm tt")>
ch8_customtag.cfmRun this example · View source
<!--- ch8_customtag.cfm: calling a custom tag --->
<CF_CH8_GREETING NAME="Frostbite Falls" COLOR="CC0000">

<CFOUTPUT><P>The tag says it greeted us at #GreetingTime#.</P></CFOUTPUT>

<!--- The same tag, called with CFMODULE and a path --->
<CFMODULE TEMPLATE="ch8_greeting.cfm" NAME="CFMODULE caller">

<!--- Variables set inside the tag stay inside the tag --->
<CFOUTPUT>
<P>Does this page see the tag's Attributes scope? #YesNoFormat(IsDefined("Attributes.Color"))#</P>
</CFOUTPUT>

CFMODULE calls the same kind of template by path (TEMPLATE="...") or by dotted name (NAME="..."), which is useful when two tags have the same name in different directories. Within a tag, ThisTag.ExecutionMode tells you whether you are running for the start tag or the end tag of a pair such as <CF_BOX> ... </CF_BOX>, and ThisTag.GeneratedContent holds the text in between.

CFX tags

When CFML is not enough (raw speed, operating system calls, a C library you already own), you can write a tag in C or C++ against the CFX API. CFX tags are registered on the CFX Tags page of the Administrator and called like any other tag, with a CFX_ prefix. KoldFusion ships with three sample CFX tags: CFX_HELLO, CFX_DICE and CFX_SYSINFO.

ch8_cfx.cfmRun this example · View source
<!--- ch8_cfx.cfm: calling CFX tags written in C --->
<P><CFX_HELLO NAME="KoldFusion developer"></P>

<!--- Ask the tag to put its result in a variable instead of the page --->
<CFX_HELLO NAME="variable" VARIABLE="Greeting">
<CFOUTPUT><P>CFX_HELLO returned: <I>#Greeting#</I></P></CFOUTPUT>

<P>Rolling three dice: <CFX_DICE ROLLS="3" SIDES="6" VARIABLE="DiceTotal"></P>
<CFOUTPUT><P>The total is #DiceTotal#.
<CFIF DiceTotal GTE 15>Lucky!<CFELSE>Better luck next time.</CFIF></P></CFOUTPUT>

Sending e-mail with CFMAIL

CFMAIL sends a message through the SMTP server configured on the Mail page of the Administrator. The body of the tag is the message, and it works like CFOUTPUT: expressions in pound signs are evaluated. Messages are written to the spool directory and delivered in the background, so the page does not wait for the mail server. With a QUERY attribute, CFMAIL sends one message per row, which is how a 1999 newsletter got out the door.

ch8_mail.cfmRun this example · View source
<!--- ch8_mail.cfm: a feedback form that e-mails the webmaster.
      Mail goes only to the local machine. --->
<CFIF IsDefined("Form.Message") AND Trim(Form.Message) IS NOT "">
  <CFPARAM NAME="Form.Topic" DEFAULT="General">
  <CFMAIL TO="webmaster@localhost"
          FROM="devguide@localhost"
          SUBJECT="Feedback: #Form.Topic#">
A visitor sent feedback from #CGI.REMOTE_ADDR# on #DateFormat(Now(), "mm/dd/yyyy")#.

Topic: #Form.Topic#

#Form.Message#
</CFMAIL>
  <P>Thank you! Your message is on its way to the webmaster
  (well, to the webmaster account on this machine).</P>
  <P><A HREF="ch8_mail.cfm">Send another</A></P>
<CFELSE>
  <H3>Send us your feedback</H3>
  <FORM ACTION="ch8_mail.cfm" METHOD="POST">
  Topic:
  <SELECT NAME="Topic">
    <OPTION>General
    <OPTION>Praise
    <OPTION>Bug Report
    <OPTION>Y2K Question
  </SELECT><BR>
  <TEXTAREA NAME="Message" ROWS="5" COLS="50" WRAP="virtual"></TEXTAREA><BR>
  <INPUT TYPE="submit" VALUE="Send feedback">
  </FORM>
</CFIF>

Note  If a message cannot be delivered it is moved to the undelivr directory under the KoldFusion install directory, and the reason is written to the mail log. Check the Mail Logging page of the Administrator when messages seem to vanish.

Where to go from here

You now know the core of CFML: templates and expressions, queries and forms, applications, errors and reusable tags. The CFML Language Reference describes every tag and function in detail, and the example applications under /CFDOCS/exampleapp/ show complete sites built from the same pieces. Happy coding, and see you on the other side of the year 2000!
